svg.title: Anthropic TriMul K1/K3 on H100: changed operations and measured results
svg.desc: K1 and K3 pipelines of the Anthropic native v5 TriMul with the three adopted changes highlighted: tanh-based sigmoid in both gates, K1 LayerNorm class 1, native bf16x2 residual add in K3. Engine-path TriMul op time drops 12.8 percent at L384 and 10.0 percent at L768 after four rounds; round 4 adds a templated mask element type in K1 and programmatic dependent launch of K1 and K3.
svg.text: Anthropic TriMul inference kernels K1/K3 · H100 optimisation (2026-09-20)

native v5 tmn90_z128_h128 · CUDA 12.9 rebuild · BF16 C128 · outgoing · residual · upstream sources untouched, 6 #ifdef switches + K3 3-WG · round 4: K1 mask element-type template + PDL · yellow = changed operation
op = K1 → cuBLAS contraction → K3 (+ mask / conversion elementwise) · 132 persistent CTAs · one launch per kernel
Engine-path TriMul op (bench.py, warm graph 5×50, same session, mean of 2 runs): L384 169.7 → 148.0 µs (−12.8%) · L768 613.8 → 552.6 µs (−10.0%) · round 3: 153.1 / 558.9
K1 · t6x32 (192 tok/CTA, 3 consumer WGs + producer WG, 512 thr)
producer: z tile TMA (48 KiB) · weight ring 8×16 KiB, resident
A fragments ← z tile (ldmatrix) → sA released at once (next tile's load overlaps)
z read 256 B/token · kept in 32 registers
LN_in · class 2 (ln_stock, reference summation order) → class 1 (ln_fragment)
bf16-z K1 was served as l2 by the tile-table name · instructions −9% · K1 −5.4%
rstd = rsqrt.approx(var+eps), y = fma((x−mean)·rstd, γ, β), one bf16 rounding (same class as K3)
8 weight blocks × WGMMA m64n64k128 (gate | proj) · two accumulator sets interleave block b+1 MMA with block b epilogue
tensor pipe 41 → 47% active (relative share grows after the change)
gate: sigmoid(g)·p·mask → sigmoid = fma(tanh.approx(0.5g), 0.5, 0.5)
original rcp.approx(1+ex2.approx(−g·log2e)): 2 MUFU, 5 dependent steps → 1 MUFU, 3 steps
XU pipe 42 → 25% · top stall 'wait' reduced · K1 −4.2%
pack bf16 → stmatrix transpose → store planes ab[2C_H][N][N]
BJ=32 tiles: TMA-store condition (BJ%64==0) unmet → per-lane lds128+stg128, named barrier per block
~23% of samples (candidate 32-token TMA store box: rejected, equal) · 512 B/token written
K1 L768: 205.9 → 183.9 µs (−10.7%) · warm NCU DRAM 62.6 → 72.3% · + resident-W wait skip
73.6% → 86% of the pattern floor (451 MB @ 2.85 TB/s = 158 µs)
K3 · t3x64 s8a1 (192 tok/CTA, 3 consumer WGs + producer, 512 thr, 160 regs) ← adopted in round 3
producer: X planes TMA (32 KiB) · z tile TMA (32 KiB, barrier per chunk) · W_og|W_o 8×8 KiB resident
X sub-tile ldmatrix.trans → sX released at once → LN_out (class 1, SERIAL affine)
X read 256 B/token · LN affine/pack ≈24% of K3 samples
z rows → gate operand: LN_in recomputed (2-pass statistics + affine, class 1)
z read 256 B/token · statistics handoff from K1 SAVE: rejected (latency-bound, §7)
4 output blocks × (proj m64n32k128 + gate m64n32k128) · two accumulator sets (a2)
tensor 20 → 22% · mbarrier waits (X/z/W) ≈11% · eligible warps 0.7/cycle (latency-bound)
o = bf16(sigmoid(g)·p) → the same tanh sigmoid
XU 21 → 12% · K3 −6.3% (K3's gate is 128 ch/token; the MUFU dependency chain is the epilogue's critical path)
numerics: 3.4% of bf16 elements differ from the original (mostly 1 ulp); rel_rms vs the fp32 reference unchanged
residual: out = bf16(z + o) → one add.rn.bf16x2 instruction
original unpack 2 + fadd 2 + cvt.rn.bf16x2 (5 instructions) → bit-identical result · K3 −3.1%
stmatrix staging → TMA bulk store per warp slice (dims [C_z][N][N]) · 256 B/token written
74.6% → 90% of the pattern floor (451 MB @ 2.85 TB/s = 158 µs)
Isolated A/B (same conditions, one process per variant, CUPTI over 60 calls · L768 K1 / K3 µs · original 205.9 / 210.8)
adopted: tanh sigmoid 195.9 / 196.4 · K1 LN class 1 193.4 / — · bf16x2 residual — / 189.6 (on comb1) → combined 185.0 / 189.6
rejected: exact variant (K3 238) · tile re-tune (default optimal) · START_OFFSET 0/4 (unchanged) · K1 BULK_STORE (inactive at BJ=32) · K3 BULK_STORE=0 (+2.5%)
rejected: K3 regs 40/232 (−1.5%, 0 combined) · K3 LN SERIAL off (+2%) · K1 SCHED 1 (L384 +3.6%) · K1 t3x64 + TMA store (equal)
cuBLAS contraction 178 µs (29% of the op) unchanged · numerics class: tolerance (fast); the exact word (reference-order K3) is a separate kernel, unchanged
payload: experiments/trimul_k1k3_inference (overlay + build_payload.py) · served through TRIMUL_NATIVE_BUILD_DIR (trimul_native.face) · production dispatch unchanged
report records/report-2026-09-20.ko.md · harness bench_op.py · raw data records/
SoL judgement
L768: essential bytes 451 MB; K1 86% / K3 90% of the streaming pattern floor 158 µs (DRAM 72–75%). L384: 78% / 73% (ragged tail). Only K1 below 90%.
Round 3: resident-W wait skip (adopted), K3 3 WG (adopted); warp-local store · paired store · gate FMA · statistics handoff · 32-token TMA store rejected by measurement (report §7–8).
Round 4 (SoL re-examined on the engine-op metric) · 2 adopted · payload: overlay with TMN_MASK_TEMPLATE + TMN_PDL
Mask element-type template (K1 names m2 = bf16, m3 = bool): removes the per-call fp32 cast kernel 4.4 / 4.9 µs, output bit-identical · a bool mask gives K1 another −4 µs at L768
PDL (griddepcontrol.wait / launch_dependents + cuLaunchKernelEx attribute): the K1 prologue (weight fan-out ≈4 µs) overlaps the K3 tail at the K3 → next-op K1 boundary · 2-op chain −1.9 µs (L384)

cuBLAS contraction: NCU DRAM 304 + 139 MB = essential bytes, DRAM 72% + tensor 78% @ 1.58 GHz (power-throttled), L384 at the memory floor · best of 8 cuBLASLt algorithms = the default → nothing to replace
Remaining structural loss (per-CTA clock probe): CTA startup fan-out K1 4.2 / K3 3.3–4.8 µs · ragged tail L768 ≈5.4 µs per kernel · SM variance · steady-state tiles at 93–95% of the streaming floor
vs the op composite floor: L768 552.6 µs = 86% · L384 148.0 µs = 81% · unimplemented candidates (each ≤2%): 64-token WG-granular tail split, 2-CTA cluster multicast weights, bool mask from the engine
